title: Hotel world
content: This is now my 3rd post in this community. I first wrote about my “mall world” followed by “school world” - now I’m here to share my “hotel world”. I find it super interesting that many of you have commented or messaged me with your own personal experiences relating to my last posts. Maybe someone can relate to this one too. Hotel world for me has several variations. One world I’ve visited several times is more like a motel.. or individual units lined up. In the middle of a busy town. The town is also a bit sketchy and it’s always very late at night. There’s vending machines outside my door and a semi-scary hall with laundry facilities. The room itself is almost completely enclosed by floor to ceiling windows with long blinds. I hate this because I feel like from certain angles strangers on the street can peek in and see me. There’s a bus stop about 2 feet from the window closest to my bed. I can see through the sliver of blinds a person waiting for the bus and it gives me the creeps. Payment for the room is done by swiping your credit card at the door knob and then the door unlocks, allowing you room access with no front desk worker. I’m always alone and never sure why I’m there in the first place. It’s almost like I’m purposely waiting for the sun to rise so I can leave and feel safe. Another hotel I often visit reminds me more of an apartment building. I’m always on the top floor with glass ceilings looking out into the moonlit sky. There’s usually a rooftop area too. There’s always more than 1 entrance into the room which makes me feel uneasy. At times, strangers use my back door to pass through to their own rooms which confuses me and makes me feel unsafe. Yet another hotel location I visit: more upscale, usually connected to something like a casino. There’s large floor to ceiling windows and I’m very high up- like 60th floor or something. Whenever I get close to the window, the room feels like it’s tilting and I have to cling to the floor to not “fall”. There’s always a community bathroom in the hall, similar to college dorms. I never spend much time in the room itself… I’m usually wandering the long wide halls or riding the very large escalators that lead to the lobby (again usually a casino setting). There’s glass elevators that go very fast. If I do end up in the casino portion, it’s dim with lots of red lighting. The slot machines are very spread apart and it’s never very busy.
